messages:
emma_support: Hi team — escalated from @sam_customer: customer is seeing streaming responses cut off mid-output on our text-generation endpoint. They get 1–3 SSE chunks, then connection closes and client reconnects. No error body, just truncated output. request id: r-9f3b2c. Seen across multiple regions.

sam_customer: Repro steps I gave them: open a simple EventSource or curl -N to our /v1/streams endpoint with a 60s idle period. They usually see the first chunk instantly, then nothing, then disconnect at ~60s. No 5xx. Happens behind their ALB + Cloudflare.

emma_support: Customer reports they already raised with infra and their ALB idle timeout is default 60s. They suspect Cloudflare/edge buffering as well. Sending logs in a sec.

raj_sre: Can you paste the raw client console log / curl output and any X-Request-Id / request-id headers? Also want the nginx/ALB logs showing the tcp connection close. This pattern looks like proxy idle drop rather than our app killing the stream.

sam_customer: CLI dump attached (paste):
```
> curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." https://api.redwood.example/v1/streaming --data-binary @- 
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.0.0.5) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/streaming HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.example\n> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0\n> Accept: */*\n> Transfer-Encoding: chunked

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< cache-control: no-cache
< connection: keep-alive

data: {"token":"tok1"}

# ~15s of output

data: {"token":"tok2"}

# then nothing, client sees EOF at ~60s with no trailing error
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```

sam_customer: ALB logs show TargetResponseTime low, but the TCP connection teardown lines match the same timestamp as the client EOF. No origin 5xx. Cloudflare shows "response buffered" events for some requests.

liam_runtime: Thanks — this is a classic mixed-proxy buffering + idle timeout interaction. Quick notes:
- If any proxy between client and origin buffers the response fully (or expects content-length), they may hold the connection open and then close if idle timer hits.
- ALB default idle timeout = 60s. If the client side expects long-lived SSE, that needs bump or heartbeat.
- Cloudflare (and some CDNs) will buffer responses for HTML/HTTP/1.1 and only flush when full chunked segments are accumulated, or if the origin sends specific headers to hint streaming.

mikaela_eng: What headers are we currently emitting? Do we send chunked Transfer-Encoding and do we flush after each write? Also, are we sending periodic SSE heartbeat comments (":\n") so the proxies see activity?

emma_support: From customer capture: response headers include content-type: text/event-stream, cache-control: no-cache, connection: keep-alive. Transfer-Encoding: chunked is present. They're not seeing heartbeat comments. App writes tokens when generated and flushes; but gaps between tokens can be >30s for long-lived completions.

liam_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: long gaps between actual data chunks + proxies that either buffer small writes or enforce a 60s idle = connection gets closed by proxy while client thinks stream is open. The partial output is delivered because early chunks made it through, then the idle kill results in an abrupt EOF and no structured error.

raj_sre: Proposed mitigations to test (in order):
1) App-level: emit lightweight SSE heartbeats every 15s (e.g., ": heartbeat\n\n") so proxies see traffic. Works without changing infra.
2) ALB: increase idle timeout to >=300s on the customer's ALB (or match expected longest gap).
3) Cloudflare: disable response buffering / enable streaming. On Cloudflare Workers/CDN you can use streaming responses or set "Cache Level: Bypass" and disable buffering at the zone/page rule level.
4) Nginx/Envoy: ensure proxy_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, chunked transfer enabled, and set keepalive_timeouts appropriately. Example nginx config snippet: 
```
location /v1/streaming {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
  proxy_read_timeout 360s;
}
```

5) Client: implement automatic reconnect with resume semantics; keep open a retry with last-event-id if idempotent.

mikaela_eng: Also note our runtime's keep-alive behavior: we flush per-token but tiny writes can still be coalesced by kernel/TCP. Adding explicit flush + heartbeat comment will be most reliable. We can also add a config flag to the runtime to emit comment heartbeats every x seconds.

emma_support: Customer tried adding a client-side reconnect loop and saw it "work" but it's noisy and they lose throughput. Can we provide a quick patch or config for them to enable server heartbeats?

liam_runtime: I'll ship a small runtime toggle in staging: default off, but we can enable heartbeat: 15s. It will write ":\n" every 15s between tokens. That should prevent most proxy idle kills. I'll also add a note to the docs about ALB+Cloudflare gotchas.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: heartbeat-feature toggle -> runtime-staging (build b-5872).

raj_sre: After deploy, recommended repro steps for the customer:
- Turn on heartbeat toggle on our side (we can enable for their org id for testing).
- From their end, set ALB idle timeout to 300s and disable Cloudflare response buffering for that route.
- Run curl -N and confirm continuous heartbeats between data tokens: you should see repeated lines beginning with ": heartbeat" even when no token is produced.

sam_customer: I'll ask them to test tomorrow and report back. Appreciate the rapid triage. Any pitfalls?

liam_runtime: Caveat: if there's an upstream proxy that rewrites headers aggressively (removes chunked), we might still see buffering. Ask them to confirm proxies preserve Transfer-Encoding: chunked and don't add Content-Length. Also watch for nginx "proxy_buffering on;" which re-chunks server stream into larger buffered blocks.

mikaela_eng: I'll follow up with a doc snippet we can paste to customers explaining: heartbeat, ALB idle timeout, Cloudflare response buffering, nginx proxy_buffering off, and client reconnect guidance.

emma_support: Great. Marking this as an ongoing escalation. I'll update ticket r-9f3b2c once customer confirms. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam_customer: FYI their Cloudflare config had "Origin Response Buffering" enabled by default. They disabled it and saw fewer truncations during quick test but still saw an occasional disconnect when our runtime had a 45s pause. So heartbeat will probably fix it permanently.

liam_runtime: Ok please keep the logs if it recurs. If we still see abrupt EOF without upstream errors, capture tcpdump on the ALB-to-origin leg and include timestamps.

emma_support: Noted. Closing thread here for now, will reopen if customer reports continuation.
